intended_object: The pivot variable X_i (for i ∈ S), regarded as an element of the valuation ring of the weight-one valuation on k(σ). Here v_S(p) = exp(−min S-weight of a monomial of p). X_i is a uniformizer of this discrete valuation ring. This reading comes from the docstring, the name and the theorems after it (`weightOneUniformizer_isUniformizer`, `weightOneUniformizer_maximalIdeal`).
explanation:
The body is the image of `X i` in `FractionRing (MvPolynomial σ k)`, together with the proof `weightOneValuation_pivot_mem` that it lies in the valuation subring. That proof holds because the valuation of X_i is exp(−1) ≤ 1. The docstring says exactly this ("The pivot, viewed as an element of the valuation subring"). The next theorem proves that this element is a uniformizer, i.e. that its valuation generates the value group. So the name `weightOneUniformizer` is justified.

This is a specific element of a specific ring, so it is not too narrow just because it is specific. The field hypothesis on k comes from the surrounding construction, which builds the valuation through a fraction-field coordinate change; the module's Scope section states this restriction on purpose. Mathlib has no counterpart, since the weight-one valuation itself is defined in this library.
